label: Hacker News: Who is hiring?
terms_note: Monthly comment threads; applications are e-mails to the poster. The Radar reads the public Firebase API; a person sends the mail.

sdks: https://firebase.google.com/docs (Firebase client libraries recommended by the HN API README for Android / iOS / web / servers)

reference.verdict: **Verdict** — has_api: **yes** (official read-only Firebase API; apply is e-mail).

endpoints.notes: `id`, `created`, `karma`, `about`, `submitted[]` (item ids, newest first; pairs of "Who is hiring?" + "Who wants to be hired?")

reference.limits: "There is currently no rate limit." (Firebase API README). Algolia's HN endpoint publishes none on the page read. - ycombinator.com/legal: users "will not engage in or use any data mining, robots, scraping or similar data gathering or extraction methods" on the Site "except as expressly authorized by Y Combinator" — the public Firebase API is the authorized channel; use it, never scrape news.ycombinator.com HTML. - HN guidelines: "Don't solicit upvotes, comments, or submissions" — the suite must not post on HN on the user's behalf. Applying is an e-mail to the address in the comment → human
mcp_sdk: Firebase client libraries (Android / iOS / web / server) — recommended by the README; not required.
No official MCP server; community HN MCP servers exist but were not verified.

adapter.rate_note: The API README states no rate limit. Two requests per second.

get_posting.note: GET /v0/item/<id>.json for one 'Who is hiring?' comment (ids are in the monthly thread's kids[]). A hiring comment has no title, so title and description both carry the comment's HTML text (its first line is usually 'Company | Role | Location'); company is the poster's HN username (`by`); time (Unix) stays in raw. A missing item answers null (invalid_input).

not_offered.search: Listing a month's postings takes two calls (GET /v0/user/whoishiring.json → submitted[] thread id, then GET /v0/item/<thread>.json → kids[] comment ids) plus one call per comment; the API has no search endpoint and the adapter maps one call per verb.
not_offered.me: No credentials and no account endpoint (read-only public API).
not_offered.apply: Applications are e-mails or links named in each comment; HN has no write API.
